rationale: The student added 7 + 6 = 13 and wrote '13' directly into the ones place, resulting in 513 instead of bundling 10 ones into 1 ten. The place-value make-a-ten piece concretely models regrouping a pile of ones (>9) into 1 ten and leftover ones.

script.focus: ten ones bundling together to become one new ten

intent: Demonstrate make-a-ten on the place-value with values [15]. Tutor points at: ten ones bundling together to become one new ten

frames.caption: Here are 15 ones. That is too many for the ones place: it can only hold 0 to 9.
Bundle ten of them. Ten ones make one ten, so the bundle moves to the tens place. 5 ones are left.
Write 1 in the tens place and 5 in the ones place: 15. One digit per place.

judgement.reasoning: The student wrote 513 for 37 + 26 because they do not realize the ones column cannot hold two digits (13) and needs to be bundled into 1 ten and 3 ones. This demo directly addresses the underlying rule that each place only holds one digit and explicitly visualizes bundling ten ones into one ten rod.
judgement.verdict: A teacher would definitely use this short demonstration to clearly explain why a place value column cannot hold two digits and how regrouping works.
